messages.author: 0f51ce4d20b0da7c
messages.subject: color data points
parts:
Dear plotters, I am a "newb" at R and even more so with ggplot2.

I am doing PCA analyses and Rdid a good job with:
xpca <- princomp(xm, scores=TRUE, cor=TRUE)
biplot(xpca)

The results are excellent, there are 50 data points and each on is numbered, as In want.
But I also want color. I want data points (for example) 1 to 20 in one color, 21 to 35 in
another color and 36 to 50 in a third color (only 3 colors needed). How do I specify this?

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: color data points
parts:
Non ggplot2 questions are a bit more appropriate elsewhere (for example stackoverflow.com). That being said, `biplot` has an argument called "col". Pass a vector that determines the color to that, et voila.

Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: color data points
parts:
The problem with Excel isn't that it's "old fashioned", rather that
it's prone to error, not reproducible, produces poor quality figures,
etc. If these aren't issues for you, and it works for your needs,
great.

Re your original question, you probably want to assign a factor
(labels) for color before plotting, e.g.:

df <- data.frame(x=1:10,y=1:10)
df$group <- cut(df$y,breaks=c(0,3,7,10))
qplot(x,y,data=df,color=group)


Ben
